This receptor is targeted by a complex compound with a specific chemical structure, and this compound is ultimately shown to have a target of FaDu. The evidence suggests a chain of molecular interactions where Canrenoic acid acts as a modulator of the receptor, which in turn influences the activity of FaDu. The integration of these pathways highlights a potential mechanism by which Canrenoic acid may exert its effects on FaDu, possibly through a direct or indirect interaction at the receptor level. The relationship is supported by a clear, albeit indirect, pathway that links the compound to the cell of interest, emphasizing the role of the receptor in mediating the biological response.
